label: GO step, confident a1 choice (not late in episode)
explanation: Fires only at GO steps (100% of mass), and only when the agent is about to choose a1: 99.8% of mass is on GO steps with action a1, and almost none on a2 choices. Within GO, it tracks a strongly a1-favoring policy (logit(a1)-logit(a2) > ~6) and a high value estimate. It fades over the episode: rare after trial ~80, near zero in trials 90-99 (value also falls late). Magnitude is larger when the previous trial was rewarded (r1 GO steps reach ~1.0 of max, r0 GO steps ~0.35), and it also rises with since_rev (an established a1 preference). It never fires at D1 or D2, on a2 choices, or on GO steps with a weak or a2-leaning policy. Uses the agent own policy logit, which it computes itself, plus episode position; no future variables. GO & action==1 alone gets recall 0.998 but precision 0.60 (F1 0.75); adding choice>6 and ep_trial<80 gives dev F1 0.87.

issues: The core claims hold. The feature fires only at GO (D1 and D2 have 0 active steps), and 99.9% of its mass is on a1 choices. (GO & model_act==1) has recall 0.999 and precision 0.60. Choice > 8.07 has an 0.78 firing rate, and below choice 2.78 there is essentially nothing. The reported test score reproduces: P 0.849, R 0.893, F1 0.871.

The magnitude claim is wrong as stated. Using mass_recall/recall as a proxy for mean activation within predicate hits (dev): on a GO step after a reward that followed no reward, P 0.97 and mean activation 1.8x the average. After two rewards in a row it is 1.36x. After three or more rewards in a row, precision falls to 0.80 and mean activation to 0.70x, about the same as after no reward (0.63x). So the top magnitude belongs to the first reward after a non-reward, and it decays across a streak of rewards: the top windows go 1.00 -> 0.80 -> 0.62, and some low-quartile r1 steps are at 0.01-0.18. 'Rewarded GO steps reach ~1.0 vs ~0.35 unrewarded' overgeneralises.

Fading over the episode is gradual, not a cliff at trial 80. Precision of GO&choice>6 by trial bin: 0-9: 0.99, 10-39: 0.95, 40-59: 0.88, 60-69: 0.74, 70-79: 0.49, 80-89: 0.26. Much of the predicate's false-positive mass is in trials 60-79, which the ep_trial<80 cutoff lets in. The data fit better as a choice threshold that rises with trial number.

A better predicate uses only observed variables: (phase == GO) & (choice > 5 + 0.06*ep_trial). Dev F1 is 0.903 (P 0.925, R 0.882). Test F1 is 0.897 (P 0.927, R 0.869, mass recall 0.948), against 0.871 for the original. That is a modest gain, so the original is a reasonable approximation.

The since-reversal claim is weak. The firing rate climbs from 0.07 to 0.18 over trials 0-19 after a reversal, but the capped since_rev=20 bin (39% of mass) is only at 0.093. That is probably confounded with episode position. 'With a high value estimate' does check out: within the predicate, value > 7.6 gives P 0.94.
